claim_text: A verified null Pun1 allele can explain nonpungency in documented backgrounds; functional Pun1 supports capsaicinoid synthesis.
applicability: Capsicum spp.; strongest allele evidence in C. annuum, C. chinense, C. frutescens
required_conditions: Exact allele, species/accession, assay method, developmental stage, and status of pAMT/CaKR1/other pathway genes.
exclusions: Functional Pun1 guarantees a particular SHU or even pungency when other pathway loci are defective.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Specific null pAMT alleles can cause nonpungency despite functional Pun1; leaky alleles can reduce capsaicinoids.
applicability: Capsicum spp.; documented alleles in C. annuum and C. chacoense
required_conditions: Exact allele sequence, splice behavior, genetic background, Pun1 status, assay protocol.
exclusions: Any pAMT variant predicts a universal percentage reduction or exact SHU.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: The documented disrupted CaKR1 allele can cause loss of pungency in the studied C. chinense material.
applicability: Validated in a C. chinense mapping population and functional assays
required_conditions: Allele identity, species, population, Pun1 and pAMT status.
exclusions: All CaKR1 variants or all chromosome-10 haplotypes determine pungency.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: CaMYB31 activity influences pathway-gene expression and capsaicinoid accumulation.
applicability: Functionally studied in C. annuum cultivars
required_conditions: Functional variant evidence, expression context, environment, pathway genotype.
exclusions: CaMYB31 genotype alone predicts pungency presence or SHU.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: PSY1 loss can alter carotenoid accumulation and fruit color; PSY2 may partially compensate.
applicability: Capsicum spp.; many alleles/accessions
required_conditions: PSY1 allele, PSY2, CCS, ZEP, pigment measurements, maturity stage.
exclusions: PSY1 alone maps universally to red versus yellow.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Functional PSY2 can support basal carotenoid production when PSY1 is absent in the studied background.
applicability: Functional evidence in C. annuum MicroPep material
required_conditions: PSY1 and CCS alleles, expression, accession, pigment profile.
exclusions: PSY2 universally causes yellow fruit.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: CCS variation is a major determinant of carotenoid composition and mature color in many backgrounds.
applicability: Capsicum spp.
required_conditions: CCS allele plus PSY1/PSY2/ZEP and pigment measurements.
exclusions: Functional CCS alone guarantees red fruit, or null CCS alone guarantees yellow/orange.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: The documented ZEP splicing mutation contributes to orange coloration in the studied material.
applicability: C. annuum SNU-mini Orange × SNU-mini Yellow population
required_conditions: PSY1 and CCS status, exact ZEP allele, accession/background.
exclusions: ZEP genotype universally distinguishes orange from yellow peppers.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: The documented CaSGR/cl allele impairs chlorophyll breakdown; ripe fruit can appear brown or green depending on carotenoids.
applicability: C. annuum chlorophyll-retainer mutant material
required_conditions: CaSGR allele, carotenoid genotype and measured pigments, maturity.
exclusions: cl alone determines one universal ripe color.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: CaGLK2 variation contributes to chlorophyll content and immature fruit color intensity.
applicability: C. annuum; studied mapping populations and accessions
required_conditions: PRR2/APRR2 state, background, stage, chlorophyll measurement.
exclusions: A single CaGLK2 allele universally yields green versus yellow fruit.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: PRR2/APRR2 variation contributes to fruit pigmentation, often jointly with CaGLK2.
applicability: C. annuum and comparative Solanaceae evidence
required_conditions: Exact allele, GLK2, PSY1/CCS, stage, population.
exclusions: PRR2 is a universal red/yellow or green/yellow switch.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: The documented CaAN3/CaPs allele contributes to purple stripe formation in the studied material.
applicability: C. annuum Chen12-4-derived mapping populations
required_conditions: Exact structural variant/transcript, tissue, developmental stage, CaAN2 and other anthocyanin regulators.
exclusions: CaAN3 alone explains all purple, black, foliage, flower, or fruit pigmentation.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Functional Bs2 can confer resistance to strains carrying recognized avrBs2.
applicability: Pepper gene; functional transfer also shown in tomato
required_conditions: Host allele, Xanthomonas species/strain, avrBs2 status, temperature/assay conditions.
exclusions: Bs2 confers universal bacterial spot resistance.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Bs3 and Bs3-E recognize distinct AvrBs3-family effectors through promoter activation specificity.
applicability: C. annuum and Xanthomonas interaction systems
required_conditions: Host promoter allele, bacterial effector allele, strain/pathovar.
exclusions: AvrBs3 is a pepper resistance gene or Bs3 gives generic disease resistance.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Named pvr1 coding alleles can confer recessive resistance to defined potyviruses by altering eIF4E–VPg compatibility.
applicability: C. annuum and C. chinense germplasm
required_conditions: Exact host allele, zygosity, virus species and strain, alternate eIF4E isoforms.
exclusions: Any pvr1 allele confers resistance to every potyvirus.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Functional Pvr4 can recognize defined potyvirus effectors and confer resistance in validated combinations.
applicability: C. annuum
required_conditions: Host allele, virus isolate/pathotype, environmental assay conditions.
exclusions: Pvr4 is universal or permanently durable against all potyvirus evolution.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Functional Tsw can confer resistance to recognized TSWV isolates.
applicability: Originally characterized/cloned from C. chinense
required_conditions: Exact host allele, virus isolate, temperature and assay conditions.
exclusions: Tsw guarantees resistance to all TSWV isolates.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: L alleles provide differential resistance spectra to tobamovirus pathotypes; L4 can be overcome by evolved PMMoV.
applicability: Multiple Capsicum species and introgressions
required_conditions: Exact L allele, virus species/pathotype, coat protein genotype, temperature.
exclusions: L4 is universally broad-spectrum or resistance cannot break.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: CMS status follows maternal cytoplasm and can be restored by compatible nuclear genes.
applicability: Primarily C. annuum breeding systems
required_conditions: Named CMS line/cytoplasm, maternal parent, Rf/Rf2/pr status, temperature.
exclusions: All pepper CMS systems share one universal mitochondrial allele or one universal Rf rule.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: CaPPR6-region haplotypes are strongly associated with restoration in defined populations.
applicability: C. annuum CMS/restorer populations
required_conditions: CMS cytoplasm, restorer source, marker validity, temperature, modifier loci.
exclusions: CaPPR6 genotype universally predicts fertility across all CMS lines.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: Rf2 contributes to fertility restoration in the reported G164 CMS system.
applicability: C. annuum G164 and 77013A-derived populations
required_conditions: Exact CMS cytoplasm, Rf1 state, G164-derived haplotype, environment.
exclusions: Rf2 is required or sufficient in every pepper CMS system.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release

claim_text: A recessive cvr4 locus confers ChiVMV resistance in the reported CV9 material.
applicability: C. annuum CV9 × Jeju population
required_conditions: Causal allele/marker, virus isolate, genetic background.
exclusions: cvr4 confers resistance to all ChiVMV isolates or other potyviruses.
review_status: Curated seed record; independent domain review required before production release
